title: Replace quality_gate.go with simplified review phase
description:
The current quality_gate.go implements the per-sub-task test→review→ux→security→fix loop.
In the new flow, this is replaced by:
1. Per-bead: QA writes tests, Coder implements until tests pass (this is in task_runner.go)
2. Post-all-beads: QA review + UX + Security run ONCE, PM arbitrates

Options:
A) Delete quality_gate.go entirely — all logic moves to task_runner.go
B) Refactor quality_gate.go into a simpler "ReviewPhase" that just runs QA+UX+Security once and returns combined feedback

Prefer option A for simplicity. Move these helpers to task_runner.go or helpers.go:
- collectProjectFiles / collectProjectFilesFromRoot
- buildTestFailure
- extractCoderResult / mergeFileList
- saveNiceToHaveFile

Delete:
- RunChecks loop
- fixAndRebuild
- applyFeedbackPolicy / issueFingerprint / splitIssues (PM handles this now)
- runPhaseIfActive / freezePhaseAfterCleanRuns
- pastIssues / cleanRuns tracking
- maybeUpdateTests (QA handles test updates directly)

title: Rewrite task_runner.go with new pipeline flow
description:
Rewrite internal/orchestrator/task_runner.go to implement the new flow:

func (tr *TaskRunner) run(ctx, input):
  1. negotiate(ctx, input) → TaskSpec (keep existing)
  2. decompose(ctx, spec) → beads/SubTasks (keep existing)
  3. executeBeads(ctx, spec, beads) — per bead:
     a. QA writes tests (TDD): qa.WriteTests()
     b. Coder implements in loop:
        - coder.Run() → build & test
        - if pass → bead done
        - if fail N times (configurable, default 3) → qa.VerifyTests()
        - if QA confirms tests correct + coder still fails → escalate to PM
  4. qualityReview(ctx, files):
     - qa.Run() (quality/logic review)
     - ux.Run() (optional)
     - security.Run() (optional)
  5. pmArbitrate(ctx, allFeedback):
     - if all clear → done
     - else → PM creates new SubTasks → goto step 3
     - PM decides reviewScope for next iteration

Remove:
- executeSinglePass (replaced by per-bead loop)
- Old quality gate integration (RunChecks call)
- runArchitectGate (architecture handled by PM description)
- Planner references

Keep:
- negotiate(), decompose() (with beads integration)
- runAgent() helper
- memory hooks
- bootstrapForTDD

New pipeline states: PipelineQATests, PipelineQAReview (replace PipelineTesting, PipelineReviewing)
Remove states: PipelineArchitecting, PipelinePlanning, PipelineFixing
close_reason: Rewrote task_runner with new QA-first flow: executeBead, qualityReview, PM arbitrate loop

title: Roll out scoped context based on shadow measurements (coder-fix additive; review hybrid)
description:
After collecting scoped_context_shadow measurements on real runs (agent=<role> vs agent=<role>-shadow est_tokens in orchestrator.log), decide and implement the actual behavior-changing wiring:

Rubber-duck guidance (validated):
- Do NOT scope the review path DESTRUCTIVELY first — it can hide bugs/vulns in un-targeted decls and the semantic index is stale post-coding. Review = measure (done via shadow), not trust, until selection recall is proven.
- Wire the CODER-FIX loop first as the safe behavior change: precise query (failure text + errorFiles), changed/error files rendered WHOLE (mandatory), scope only ADDITIONAL related context; missing context costs a retry, not a hidden bug. Fallback to current behavior when semantic search unavailable/empty.
- If enabling any review scoping later, use HYBRID: never remove changed/diff files; whole-render them, scope only additional related files. Consider role-specific queries (QA/Security/UX).
- Address index staleness: refresh index post-coding or treat changed files as mandatory whole seeds.

Gate: enable a mode by default only if real-run tokens drop AND review/QA quality holds. Depends on shadow measurement infra (...-kuf, done). Coordinate with precision follow-ups ...-700. Parent epic ...-40i.

title: Wire scoped context into agents behind a flag + measure on real tasks
description:
Spike ...-5vk returned GO: symbol-scoped rendering cut tokens ~98% with recall of task-relevant decls 0->1 on the rendering dimension. Productionize:

1. Wire query -> ProjectContext.SemanticSearchSymbols(query,k) -> targets map -> buildScopedSourceContext(targets) in the per-agent context assembly (review agents via buildCompactSourceContext; coder fix paths). Put behind a config flag (default off) so it can be A/B'd.
2. Use the existing source_context instrumentation (component=source_context) to compare est_tokens and (where ground truth exists) recall between scoped and whole-file on REAL pipeline runs, not just the synthetic fixture.
3. Evaluate TARGET-SELECTION quality: the spike isolated rendering; real gains depend on SemanticSearchSymbols picking the right symbols. Measure recall of edited decls when targets come from the embedder, not an oracle. If selection recall is poor, prefer a hybrid (scoped for high-confidence hits, whole-file fallback).
4. Decide rollout: enable by default per-agent only if real-run tokens drop AND review/QA quality holds.

Depends on spike ...-5vk (done). Coordinate with precision follow-ups ...-700. Parent epic ...-40i.

title: Spike: ranked declaration-chunk context vs expandWithGraph
description: Minimal proof-of-value (NO persistence, NO post-commit hook, NO full callgraph): given a task prompt + seed files, produce a ranked list of declaration CHUNKS (semantic hits + AST refs) instead of files, render under budget, and compare input tokens + recall of actually-edited chunks against current expandWithGraph. Success criteria: clearly fewer tokens AND equal-or-better recall@budget of edited/tested code at acceptable latency. If it does not clearly win, STOP here and do not build persistence. Parent: ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-40i.

title: AST/type-aware CallersOf + symbol references (replace token grep)
description: Replace internal/context/graph.go CallersOf (naive token mention) with AST/type-aware package-local reference search via go/packages: definitions, imports, references, method receivers, direct static calls. Keep ON-DEMAND (no persistence), cache by file hash in-process. Must degrade gracefully on parse errors / dirty workspace (agents edit mid-run). Frame as 'typed references / approximate calls', not a precise callgraph. Parent: ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-40i.

title: Render selected declaration chunks (symbol-level) in buildSourceContextSized
description: Extend the source-context builder to accept {file, chunk/symbol} targets and render ONLY selected declarations (plus package header/import block, enclosing type for methods, directly-referenced const/var/type) instead of whole files. chunker already splits Go files into decl chunks; selection is currently file-first. This is the highest-ROI part per rubber-duck and does NOT need a graph DB. Parent: ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-40i.

title: Instrument source-context assembly (tokens/files/chunks/selection reason)
description: Add visibility into what buildSourceContextSized produces, to measure before building anything. Track: input chars/tokens of rendered context per agent; number of files and chunks included; per-entry selection reason (seed / import / caller / semantic-hit / caller-supplied); context-build latency. Emit via the bus / logging so it can be compared across runs. This is the prerequisite for evaluating any scoped-context change. Offline eval idea: replay past tasks with known diffs and compute recall@budget of edited files/chunks and irrelevant-token ratio. Parent: ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-40i.

title: Scoped code-graph context for agents (service map)
description:
Reduce per-agent input-token cost and improve relevance by assembling SCOPED, symbol/chunk-level source context instead of whole files. Inspired by graphify (knowledge graph), but adapted to this project's 'no hidden multi-session state' principle: an explicit context-assembly layer, not a model session.

Current state: agents run as one-shot CLI processes; each gets a freshly assembled prompt, so the same files/plan are re-sent repeatedly (large \xE2\x86\x93 input tokens in the System Monitor). Context is built by internal/agent/source_context.go (buildSourceContextSized) which renders WHOLE files (chunk-truncated) until a char budget. A crude graph already exists: internal/context/graph.go (ImportsOf, CallersOf=naive token match, PrimarySymbolOf) used by expandWithGraph.

Rubber-duck verdict: a persistent go/packages+callgraph graph DB is OVER-ENGINEERED as a first move and risky (staleness vs uncommitted edits; CHA/RTA noise). Build the lean version first; persist only if metrics justify it.

Lean sequence (tracked as child issues):
1. Instrumentation of source-context (tokens, files, chunks, why selected).
2. Chunk/symbol-level rendering in buildSourceContextSized.
3. AST/type-aware CallersOf (replace token grep), on-demand + in-process hash cache.
4. Semantic search returns chunk/symbol IDs, not just files.
5. Spike: ranked declaration-chunk context (semantic hits + AST refs) vs current expandWithGraph; compare tokens/relevance.
6. ONLY persist a graph if repeated runs show measurable wins.

Boundary: memory = durable facts over time; service map = derived, disposable cache of the current source tree (sibling DB .orchestrator/index/, never memory facts).

title: Improve symbol-chunk selection precision (grouped decls, qualified methods, signature refs)
description:
Follow-ups from rubber-duck review of symbol-scoped rendering (sgm). Deferred because they need chunker/target-model changes best co-designed with the evaluation spike (5vk):

1. Grouped declarations: chunker.classifyGoDecl uses firstSpecName, so 'type ( A; B )' / grouped const/var become ONE chunk named after the first spec. Requesting B won't match; requesting A over-includes B; a method on B can't pull B's type. Fix: split grouped GenDecls into per-spec chunks OR store all declared names per chunk and match any.
2. Qualified method targets: bare method name (e.g. 'Close') matches every method of that name across receiver types and pulls each enclosing type. Support structured/qualified targets like (*Server).Start or {kind,recv,name}; keep bare-name as fallback.
3. Signature-referenced local types: selecting a function does NOT pull local types in its signature (e.g. func NewServer(cfg Config) (*Server,error) omits Config/Server). Pull directly-referenced local types from selected function/method signatures at minimum.

Parent: ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-40i. Coordinate with ai-coding-agents-orchestrator-5vk (spike) and -y3t (AST-aware refs).

title: Semantic search returns chunk/symbol IDs (not only files)
